resources.string: Checks which apps are really on screen (package names only) so Pausely can show its pause and limit screens. It never reads text, messages or passwords, and nothing leaves your phone.

No apps yet. Tap + Add app.

• Uses Android\'s Accessibility service to see which apps are on screen (only their package names) and to show Pausely\'s pause and block screens. • Never reads what is written on your screen, your messages or passwords. • Nothing leaves your phone. The app has no internet permission. • Android will describe this permission as \"retrieve window content\"; Pausely only uses it to know which app is open. • You can turn it off any time in Settings → Accessibility.
Too many fails. Try again in %1$d min.
Tap the COLOR of the word, not what it says (%1$d/5)
%1$d min per app. Apps can override it with their own limit (tap an app card).
A 5-second breather before a limited app opens.
Every limit shrinks by 1 min per week, down to a floor of 5 min.

Pausely runs entirely on your phone. It has no internet permission and sends nothing anywhere.

It uses the Accessibility service only to learn which apps are on screen (package names), so it can time your use and show pause/block screens. Android words this as "retrieve window content", but Pausely never reads text, messages or passwords.

It requests no permissions at all.

Stored locally: your app list, limits, schedules, 30 days of per-app usage minutes and open counts, and a log of your last 20 counted sessions. Uninstalling removes it.

Questions: srikrishna.ayyanki@gmail.com

string-array.name: guide_titles
string-array.item: 1. Install the APK
2. Play Protect says \"App blocked\"
3. Allow restricted settings
4. Turn on the service
5. Choose apps and limits
6. Emergency unlock
7. Keep it alive / save battery
8. The floating shortcut
Troubleshooting

string-array.name: guide_bodies
string-array.item: Open the APK from Files/Drive. If Android asks, allow \"Install unknown apps\" for that app.
Play Store → profile icon → Play Protect → ⚙ → turn OFF \"Scan apps with Play Protect\" (or pause it). Install the APK, then you can turn it back on. If it blocks again later, repeat.
Android greys out accessibility for sideloaded apps. Tap \"Open App info\" below → ⋮ (top right) → \"Allow restricted settings\" → confirm PIN/fingerprint.
Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps → Pausely → ON → Allow. It only detects which app is in front. Nothing is recorded off-device and the app has no internet permission.

Set a default limit in Settings. On the home screen tap + Add app; tap an app card to give it its own limit or a schedule. Raising a limit, removing an app or loosening a schedule needs a puzzle on purpose. Lowering is free.
Tap an app card → Emergency +5 min. Once a day, shared by all apps, puzzle + 30 s wait. It does not lift schedule blocks.
Settings → Apps → Pausely → Battery → Unrestricted. Some phones (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, OnePlus) otherwise kill the service; also allow Autostart there. Pausely uses no background polling.

After you enable Pausely, Android 13+ may show a small floating accessibility button. Tap it for a quick panel: today\'s usage, −5 min on any limit, pause-screen and reduction toggles. To hide it: Settings → Accessibility → Accessibility button (or Pausely → Shortcut) → off.

• Counter stays 0: service is off or restricted (steps 3-4).
• Stopped working after an update: toggle the service off and on.
• Install updates over the old version; don't uninstall, or you lose usage data.
• Daily usage resets at midnight.
